PC-style skeleton with separating sets

Source: R/cpdag.R
mc_pc_skeleton.Rd

Constraint-based skeleton discovery from a between-response covariance matrix. Starting from the complete graph, an edge \(i - j\) is deleted as soon as a conditioning set \(S\) of adjacent nodes makes the partial correlation \(\rho_{ij \cdot S}\) non-significant, and that set is stored as the separating set of the pair. The neighborhoods are frozen within each conditioning order and both endpoint neighborhoods are examined, as in the order-independent skeleton stage of the PC-stable algorithm (Colombo and Maathuis, 2014), a variant of the PC algorithm (Spirtes, Glymour and Scheines, 2000; Kalisch and Buehlmann, 2007).

Usage

mc_pc_skeleton(Sigma, n, alpha = 0.05, max_ord = NULL, df_residual = NULL)

Arguments

Sigma

an \(R \times R\) covariance matrix of the responses, e.g. fit$graph$Shat.

n

number of experimental units, taken as independent.

alpha

significance level of the Fisher z test of a zero partial correlation, a single number strictly between zero and one.

max_ord

maximum size of the conditioning set; NULL uses \(R - 2\).

df_residual

optional residual degrees of freedom \(\nu_e\) from the first-stage fit, as a number or as the result of mc_residual_df. When supplied, the Fisher factor uses \(\nu_e - |S| - 2\); otherwise it uses \(n - |S| - 3\).

Value

A list with the symmetric integer adjacency matrix of the skeleton (one for an edge, zero otherwise); the sepset list of length \(R^2\), whose elements (i - 1) * R + j and (j - 1) * R + i hold the integer vector of nodes that separated \(i\) from \(j\), integer(0) for the empty set, and NULL when the pair was never separated; the df_residual used; and diagnostics, a list with the number of tests (n_tests), the number of ridge-regularized blocks (n_regularized), the largest ridge (max_ridge), the smallest Fisher degrees of freedom (min_df) and the contract used (df_contract).

The test

The partial correlation \(\hat\rho_{ij\cdot S}\) is read off the inverse of the \((i, j, S)\) block of Sigma and clamped to \([-0.999999, 0.999999]\) before Fisher's transform \(z=\operatorname{atanh}(\hat\rho_{ij\cdot S})\sqrt{n-|S|-3}\) (with \(\nu_e-|S|-2\) in place of \(n-|S|-3\) when df_residual is given), so that a perfectly collinear block gives a large but finite statistic. A pair is declared conditionally uncorrelated, and its edge removed, when the two-sided normal p-value of \(z\) is at least alpha. A block that is nearly singular is inverted after a ridge of \(10^{-8}\) times its scale and the event is counted in diagnostics; a conditioning order whose Fisher degrees of freedom are not positive, or a block that gives no valid partial correlation even after the ridge, is an error. Because Sigma is usually computed from the estimated residuals of responses that need not be Gaussian, the normal reference for \(z\) is a working asymptotic calibration and not an exact one. The factor takes n as the number of independent units, the rows of the data for a fit with an identity within-response structure. There is no cluster argument: with dependent rows, n overstates the information and the test is anti-conservative.

References

Spirtes, P., Glymour, C. and Scheines, R. (2000). Causation, Prediction, and Search, 2nd edition. MIT Press.

Kalisch, M. and Buehlmann, P. (2007). Estimating high-dimensional directed acyclic graphs with the PC-algorithm. Journal of Machine Learning Research 8, 613-636.

Colombo, D. and Maathuis, M. H. (2014). Order-independent constraint-based causal structure learning. Journal of Machine Learning Research 15, 3921-3962.

See also

mc_separating_sets, mc_find_vstructures, mc_graph_pipeline

Examples

set.seed(1); n <- 600
z1 <- rnorm(n); z2 <- rnorm(n); z3 <- 0.7 * z1 + 0.7 * z2 + rnorm(n)
S <- cov(cbind(z1, z2, z3))
mc_pc_skeleton(S, n)$adjacency
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3]
#> [1,]    0    0    1
#> [2,]    0    0    1
#> [3,]    1    1    0
